name: Optical speed
source: Goldman Sachs optical note (04-17-2026) + Arista Q1 FY2026 (05-05-2026)
note: Optical interconnect speed migration (per-lane and per-port roadmap).

tables.title: Speed roadmap
rows: Mainstream 2024 -> declining 2025-27; 'going to be around for quite a while - they just don't go away'; multiple nodes run in parallel (Viavi Q4 FY2026)
Mainstream 2025-26; still the BIGGEST VOLUME DRIVER in mid-2026 and 'a big driver for a long time' - large installed base being upgraded; may pull back after 1.6T parity (Viavi Q4 FY2026)
Mainstream 2027; ramping very quickly into PRODUCTION - reaching PARITY with 800G in 2027, then taking the lead (Viavi Q4 FY2026)

tables.title: Adoption by hyperscaler
rows: NVIDIA, Google, Microsoft, Meta, Amazon, Oracle, Chinese CSPs
NVIDIA & Google now; Meta 2026; Microsoft / Amazon / Oracle 2027

tables.title: Connector / form-factor roadmap (Arista view)
tables.note: Arista Q1 FY2026 (05-05-2026): OSFP shaped the last decade; XPO expected to shape the next.
rows: Remains fine at 400G and 800G; runs out of steam at higher speeds
12.8 Tbps/module, 204.8 Tbps per OCP rack unit, 400W integrated cold plate; >100 vendor endorsements; "ten-year run"
Preferred for 2-3 m reach inside scale-up racks

Arista rejects ~5 proprietary CPO implementations, committing to ONE OPEN CPO: socketed optical engines + pigtail fibers, pre-tested modules, multi-vendor interface (a.k.a. NPO); trials next year; 'majority of the world stays PLUGGABLE + COPPER; some CPO in 2028-29' (Arista Q2 FY2026)
Ethernet scale-up spec; Arista scale-up entry 2027+ (5-7 rack designs in active engineering); 1.6T at production scale 2027
